HubSpot Company Record — HelioSearch (heliosearch.ai)

Summary
- Self-serve Hosted API customer (embeddings-heavy). Scaling quickly; signal flagged for high throughput + EU region.
- Primary ask: predictable throughput and EU data residency; exploring Redwood Dedicated in eu-west for embeddings.

Firmographics / ICP notes
- HQ: EU (team split Berlin + Amsterdam per call)
- Product: hosted semantic search / RAG infra for B2B SaaS; embed customer docs + tickets + knowledge bases.
- Buying motion: engineering-led; security review early because their customers are regulated (FinTech + B2B SaaS).

PLG → Sales trigger context (why this account surfaced)
- Signal: sustained embeddings volume increase (30d) + high concurrency spikes during nightly re-index.
- Signal: region preference indicates EU routing; repeated console visits to region/residency docs.
- Internal note: not a "contact sales" submission; this is usage/intent-based routing.

Workload & technical requirements (from discovery notes)
- Workload type: embeddings (bulk indexing + real-time incremental updates)
- Patterns:
  - Nightly batch re-index: heavy throughput burst; they want this to finish within a fixed window.
  - Daytime: steady low-latency embed for incremental doc updates.
- Targets (rough / needs validation):
  - Batch: "we can tolerate higher latency per request, but need the job done by morning" (paraphrase)
  - Online: p95 latency sensitivity for incremental updates; wants stable queueing under load.
- Model flexibility: open to Redwood-recommended embedding models; wants ability to pin versions and avoid surprise drift.
- Cost: monitoring unit costs closely; asked for guidance on batching/caching and any Optimize recommendations.

Deployment / residency
- Preference: EU processing (eu-west). They explicitly asked whether any tokenization/log processing happens outside EU.
- Not asking for on-prem. Dedicated in eu-west likely sufficient if we can commit to residency + retention controls.

Security / compliance notes
- Needs: SOC2 evidence, audit logs availability, retention controls. Not requesting SSO/SAML yet, but likely later if they move to enterprise procurement.
- Quote (approx): "We need to be able to tell our customers where inference happens and what gets logged."

Pipeline / stage rationale
- Stage: Discovery
  - We have initial requirements and sizing questions; no formal demo completed yet.
  - Next is SE-led technical deep dive + Dedicated sizing + PoC plan.

Timeline (recent activity)
- 2025-02-18 — Company created via PLG signal routing (EU + throughput). Owner: Lukas Meyer (EMEA).
- 2025-02-20 — SDR (Rohan Mehta) sent light-touch outreach referencing scaling embeddings + EU region option (no assumptions about their stack).
- 2025-02-26 — Intro call scheduled; Markus Klein added for SE coverage.
- 2025-03-03 — Meeting booked from signal workflow; pre-read requested (throughput goals, regions, current vendor costs). Linked: thread_2025_03_03_meeting-booked-from-signal.
- 2025-03-06 — Discovery call held (notes summarized above). Discussed Dedicated in eu-west conceptually; agreed to follow up with sizing questions and a PoC outline.

Open questions (to answer in SE deep dive)
- Current embeddings model(s) + dimension + average input length distribution.
- Batch job characteristics: total documents, update frequency, concurrency they can drive, and deadline window.
- Online path: required p95/p99 latency and acceptable retries/backpressure.
- Data retention expectations: request/response logging on/off; how long; audit log access requirements.
- Region: EU-only processing requirement vs "EU preferred".

Proposed next steps
- Markus (SE) to run a 45-min technical deep dive (throughput sizing + latency SLOs).
- Lukas to send Dedicated eu-west sizing strawman + pricing packaging guidance (commit options) after confirming volumes.
- Share Redwood security evidence pack checklist (SOC2, logging, retention). (If needed, loop in Naomi Feldman / Dr. Aisha Rahman for residency language.)

Internal notes
- This account feels like a clean Dedicated candidate: predictable burst throughput + EU region preference. Keep outreach crisp; avoid over-promising on absolute latency until we confirm batch sizes and concurrency.
- If procurement accelerates, consider pulling in Jasmine Liu for governance/suppression alignment (expansion-style motion even though originated via PLG signal).
